rights.repositoryPolicy: Do not commit the source video, decoded source frames, contact sheets, or GIFs derived from this source without separate written permission.

analysisCopy.construction: Byte-for-byte concatenation of the HLS initialization fragment fileSequence0.mp4 and media fragments fileSequence1.m4s through fileSequence31.m4s in playlist order.

transition.description: Portrait outer display blurs as the device unfolds; a sharp inner-display aperture expands from the right of the moving seam, followed by a blur-resolution tail on the left pane.

foldStart.definition: Last frame with no repeatable transition blur or aperture separation.

firstAltered.definition: First frame whose right-side icon band crosses below 90 percent of the preceding clean frame's Sobel edge energy.

firstClearInnerAperture.definition: First frame with a clearly separable sharp inner-display aperture to the right of the moving fold seam.

fullAperture.definition: First frame where the physical display aperture has reached its final observed width; the left pane is still visibly blurred.

foldComplete.definition: First frame of three consecutive frames with visually stable geometry and left-pane edge energy within a 1.4 percent range.

blurEvidence.method: Mean Sobel magnitude in the fixed source-pixel ROI x=365..404, y=120..234 for blur onset; x=200..289, y=90..249 for final left-pane stability.
blurEvidence.limitations: The ROIs are source-pixel measurements from a produced camera shot. Physical motion, occlusion, editorial motion blur, and H.264 compression prevent treating these values as direct UI blur radii.

boundarySamples.method: Manual source-pixel annotation of the moving seam and current right display edge. Visible aperture is their horizontal distance, normalized by the 282-pixel aperture observed at frame 348.

transition.voidObservation: This opening shot has no rising black void. Its corresponding measurable boundary is the near-vertical fold seam and expanding sharp aperture. A MacBook comparison may rotate the fold-axis coordinate, but must label that as an axis-normalized analogy rather than a literal void match.
